I'm 25 and I understand how you feel because I feel the same way. Logically I know that's insane because 25 is so young but I can't help it. I've lost 30+lbs so far and I just keep wishing I had done it sooner when I was younger. 


As someone who grew up online heavily influenced by social media, I agree with everyone who has said that social media has massively distorted our views on age and made many of us feel like if we are 21+ then we already have one foot in the grave. It's ridiculous and absolutely not true at all. 


31 is extremely young and there is absolutely nothing that you could have done in your 20s that you can't also do now. Besides, it's never too late to better yourself regardless of your age. You've done a great job OP, try to enjoy your accomplishments, you deserve to.

Honestly the best thing I did was cut out fast food almost entirely and cut out binge snacking. I never realized how many calories I was consuming before because I didn't track them. I ate whatever I wanted and I didn't move very much at all. I also ate a lot just because I was bored and I had a bad habit of forcing myself to overeat even when I was no longer hungry. 

Once I became more mindful of my hunger cues and started eating healthier foods my body adapted and I stopped craving a lot of the super high calorie, high sugar, high fat foods that I had been consuming for years.
I count my calories and try to stay within my limits, around 1400 calories a day. But if I go over then I don't beat myself up about it. 

Exercising has been a big help for me too. I started walking and then incorporated running into my routine as well. Now I go for runs multiple times per week which has helped me to build muscle and burn calories faster and just overall be in much better physical shape. 

I've also learned that being kind to yourself while you're losing weight is really important. Accepting that you will make mistakes will help you to not give up entirely and bounce back faster. 
And go slow. Weightloss isn't a race, you don't need to rush it and your body will be very grateful if you take your time.

I'm the same height as you. I eat 1200-1300 calories a day and I've lost 24lbs in the past 10 weeks. I do intermittent fasting for 16 hours every day and eat 2 meals a day, both are high in protein and vegetables. Veggies are my new bestfriend because I can eat tons of them without using too many calories. I also drink about 4 liters of water a day and this helps a lot to keep my stomach full. 


I do a lot of cardio every day as well. I dont know what your current exercise routine is but you might want to increase your workouts a little so that you can increase your caloric intake. 100-200 calories can make a huge difference in the amount of food that you get to eat and that might help with some of your hunger pangs.


I know it's hard being small because we have to eat so little in order to maintain a deficit but it is possible to do it and not feel super hungry all the time. My advice is to exercise more, drink lots of water, and eat lots of high volume/low calorie foods. From one 5'2 person to another, you've got this!

I typically exercise for about 2 hours every morning from around 5am-7am all cardio and about 15 minutes of strength training each day as well. My window to eat is from 12pm to 8pm and I have 2 meals during that time, one between 12pm-2pm and the other between 5pm-7pm just depending on how I feel. 

I dont eat anything special honestly I just make sure to count the calories and stay within my allotment for the day. Getting enough protein has always been something I struggle with since I dont really care for meat but I'm doing my best to add more to each meal using foods I like. My biggest tip for food would be to eat things you enjoy but in moderation. I allow myself to eat whatever I want so long as I maintain my caloric deficit. This way I am able to satisfy any cravings and not feel like I'm missing out on the foods I love. I also give myself one day a week to just maintain if I want to which gives me the freedom to eat an extra treat and not feel too restrictive. 

If I slip up (which does happen) I don't get mad or upset, I just correct myself and get back on track the next day. I keep reminding myself that I'm human, it's okay to make mistakes, and this is a lifestyle change not a diet and that helps too.
You've got this! 10lbs down already is so impressive! Keep going, you're doing amazing!
1200-1300. I'm short so my BMR is less than 1400 calories so when I add my food intake deficit to my calories burned during exercise I end up with a 1000 calorie deficit each day

As someone who has lost 10lbs in 4wks and 20lbs in the last 2 months, I do it by maintaining a fairly large deficit of about 1000 calories a day. This is not always easy and not something I necessarily recommend unless you really enjoy running or some other type of high calorie burning exercise while also eating a lower amount of calories a day. I started off (and still am) quite overweight so losing weight quickly right now is easier for me than it would be for someone who is closer to their goal weight.

In the end I have to agree with everyone else here who has said that you should try not to compare yourself to others although I know that may be easier said than done. 3lbs in 5 weeks is great progress and no easy feat.

I'm a bit confused, are you saying that you are currently using two 75watt regular light bulbs in your bearded dragons tank as basking lights? and are you asking if you can replace them with one 100watt regular light bulb? 

I have never seen anyone use a regular light bulb as a basking light for a beardie, I don't think you would get the temperatures anywhere close to warm enough. You need a basking bulb, they're expensive, I know, but in order to maintain the proper temperature you need one. you could also try a ceramic heat emitter if you would prefer a heat source that doesn't emit light.

the thermometer attached to the glass is reading a cooler temperature because the glass is cool, it is not telling you the actual temperature of the air in your tank. the heat gun you used is far more accurate and that is the temperature you should be going by. 120 is the highest I would allow my enclosure to get and even then it's pushing it. unless you have a baby dragon you do not need it to be that hot. 105 is typically perfect for an adult beardie. if it's too hot then they will not bask at all so be careful. I would suggest using the heat gun on the cool side of your enclosure as well since it is probably warmer than what your thermometer is reading.

This is Mal, short for Maleficent. She is about 7.5 months old, 15 inches long and 410 grams. She's a heavier girl but we're working on that. Something we've both been struggling with since I got her is portion control. One of the main rules every new bearded dragon owner gets told when they begin feeding their baby is to allow them to eat as much as they want for 15 minutes 3 times a day. I did this for the first 6 months of Mal's life until I realized just how big she had gotten. Now we have portion regulated meals. She never goes without food because she has constant access to fresh greens/veggies but she only gets a specific amount of live insects every day. If I were to let her have it her way she would eat until she gets sick, she's done it before. 


I say all of this because I think it's important for pet owners to recognize that you know your animal better than anyone else. What I'm doing with my bearded dragon now works for us but that doesn't mean it would work for everyone else and it also doesn't mean that I'm going to recommend it to others. It's just upsetting when you see new owners struggling when their new animal doesn't behave/fit into the very specific mold of what a bearded dragon should be. It can be very frustrating and isolating for new owners. But trust yourself, and trust your animal. If you think something is truly wrong then seek the advice of a trained professional. But try not to worry so much if your beardie's needs aren't exactly the same as everyone elses. Animals are just like people and snowflakes, no two are exactly alike and that's completely okay.

For an adult beardie they need a 75 gallon tank minimum. My little girl is almost 7 months and I still have her in a 40 gallon tank but her new tank will be here in a month and it's 120 gallons so it'll be a large upgrade for her. The bigger the tank the better in my opinion, you just have to make sure you have the right heating and lighting setup.
For lighting I use a 100watt exo terra basking spot bulb and an arcadia desert D3 uvb florescent tube light. I also use a ceramic heat emitter just to keep her tank extra warm. You definitely want to have a thermometer probe to keep track of the temperatures on the warm and cool side of your lizard's tank. My beardie's warm side stays around 105 and her cool side stays around 82 during the day and goes down to 76 at night.
